﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die in their sleep.﴾ That is: He seizes them from the bodies, by cutting off their attachment to them and their control over them, either outwardly and inwardly, as at death, or outwardly only, as in sleep.

﴿Then He withholds the one for which He has decreed death﴾ and does not return it to the body. It is also read as (quḍiya) in the passive form, with (al-mawt) in the nominative. ﴿And He sends the other back﴾ that is, the sleeping soul, to its body at the time of waking.

﴿For a term appointed﴾ is the time set for its death. It is the limit for the genus of sending (al-irsal) that occurs after the withholding, not for an individual instance of it, since that is not something that has extension or quantity. What is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that in the son of Adam there is a breath (nafs) and a spirit (ruh), between which is like the ray of the sun, so the nafs is that by which there is reason and discernment, and the ruh is that by which there is breath and movement; so both are taken at death, and the nafs alone is taken at sleep, is close to what has been mentioned.

﴿Surely in that﴾ that is, in what has been mentioned of the taking in both ways, and the withholding in one of them, and the sending in the other, ﴿are signs﴾ wondrous and indicating the perfection of His power, His wisdom, and the comprehensiveness of His mercy.

﴿for a people who reflect﴾ on the manner of the soul's attachment to bodies, and its being taken from them at times completely, as at death, and its being withheld remaining and not perishing with their perishing, and what befalls it of happiness and misery; and at other times only from their outward functions, as in sleep, and its being sent back from time to time until the completion of their terms.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 43:

﴿Or have they taken﴾ i.e., rather, the Quraysh have taken ﴿besides Allah﴾, besides His permission, the Exalted, ﴿intercessors﴾ who intercede for them with Him, the Exalted.

﴿Say: "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ The hamza (interrogative particle) is for denying the actual state of affairs and deeming it abhorrent, and for rebuking them for it. That is: say, "Do you take them as intercessors even though they possess nothing of anything, and do not understand it, let alone being able to possess intercession with Allah, the Exalted?" Or it is for denying the occurrence and negating it, with the intended meaning being to show that what they did does not amount to taking intercessors in any respect, since it is a consequence of the idols being intercessors, and that is the most evident of impossibilities. So the supposed element then differs from what was supposed at first. In either case, the "wa" (and) is a conjunction upon a conditional clause that has been omitted, because of the indication of what is mentioned, i.e.: "Would they intercede if they possessed something, and even if they possess nothing...?" The answer to "law" (even if) is omitted, because of the indication of what is mentioned concerning it, and its verification has been discussed repeatedly.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 44:

﴿Say﴾ after their rebuke and their being shown to be ignorant of what has been mentioned, as a confirmation of the truth: ﴿To God belongs all intercession.﴾ That is: He is its owner. No one can intercede at all unless the one being interceded for is one with whom He is pleased, and the intercessor has been given permission. Both of these conditions are absent here. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ is an affirmation and emphasis of this. That is: to Him belongs their dominion and whatever creatures are in them. No one can speak about any of His affairs without His permission and approval.

﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, not to anyone other than Him, neither independently nor in partnership. So on that Day He will do what He wills.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 45:

﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned﴾ apart from their gods, ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil﴾. That is: they are constricted and repelled, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn on their backs in aversion﴾.

﴿And when those other than Him are mentioned﴾, individually or together with the mention of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾, due to the extent of their infatuation with them and their forgetfulness of the right of Allah, exalted is He. The two ugly states of theirs are described with great emphasis, in that He mentioned the extreme degree of each of them. For istibshar (rejoicing) is that the heart becomes filled with joy until the surface of the face is expanded by it, and al-ishmi'zaz (recoiling) is that one becomes filled with rage and distress, from which the skin of the face contracts. The governing element (al-'amil) of the first "idha" is "ishma'azzat" (recoiled), and of the second is what governs the "idha" of suddenness (idha al-fuja'iyya), its implied sense being: at the time when those other than Him are mentioned, they suddenly rejoice at the time of rejoicing.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 46:

﴿Say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed."﴾ That is: turn to Him, exalted is He, in supplication, since you have been perplexed regarding the matter of the call (da'wah) and have grown weary because of the severity of their obstinacy (shakimah) in stubbornness (mukabarah) and opposition ('inad). For He is the One Able over things in their entirety, and the One who knows the conditions in their totality.

﴿You judge between Your servants concerning that in which they used to differ.﴾ That is: a judgment that every stubborn opponent must accept and to which every rebellious tyrant submits, and it is the punishment of this world (al-'adhab al-dunyawi), or of the Hereafter (al-ukhrawi). And His, exalted is He, saying:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 47:

﴿And if those who have wronged had everything that is on the earth, all of it...﴾ . . . etc. This is a resumptive statement (kalam mustanaf), brought to explain the consequences of the judgment that the Prophet (ﷺ) invoked, and the extent of its severity and dreadfulness; that is, even if they possessed all the wealth and treasures that are in the world.

﴿And the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾ That is: they would make all of that a ransom (fidyah) for their own selves from the severe punishment. "But it is too late (hayhat), and there is no escape (wa-la-ta hina manas)." This, as you see, is a severe threat (wa'id shadid), and a despairing of them of deliverance (iqnat).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 48:

﴿And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not been reckoning.﴾ That is: there will become apparent to them, from among the varieties of punishments, what was not in their reckoning. This is an utmost extent of threat, beyond which there is no further extent, and its counterpart is in the promise. His Exalted saying: ﴿So no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾.

﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned﴾: the evil of their deeds or their earnings, when their records are presented to them.

﴿And there will befall them that which they used to mock﴾: that is, its recompense will encompass them.

﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us.﴾ This is a report about the species in terms of what most of its individuals do. The الفاءُ (al-fa', the conjunctive particle "fa") indicates the sequence of what follows it, namely the contradiction and reversal, in relation to the two ugly states mentioned earlier. What lies between them is a parenthetical clause that emphasizes the denunciation of them, meaning: they recoil from the mention of God alone, and rejoice at the mention of the gods. So when harm touches them, they call upon the One whose mention they recoiled from, not the ones whose mention they rejoiced in.

﴿Then when We bestow upon him a favour from Us﴾ means We give it to him as a bounty, for التخويل (al-takhwil, bestowal) is specific to this sense and is not applied to what is given as a reward.

﴿He says: "I have only been given it because of knowledge."﴾ That is: because of knowledge on my part of the ways of acquiring it, or because I know that I will be given it due to my own deservingness, or because of knowledge from God regarding me and my deservingness. The الهاءُ (al-ha', the pronoun "it") is in the masculine form because the relative clause is understood in that way; otherwise, it would refer to نِعْمَةٌ (ni'mah, favour). The masculine form is used because what is meant is a thing that is a favour.

﴿Rather, it is a trial﴾ means a test and a trial for him: will he give thanks, or will he disbelieve? This is a rejection of what he said, and the change of wording serves to intensify this, and to indicate that this is not of the type of giving that signifies honour, but rather is a matter entirely distinct from it. The feminine pronoun (in هي, "it") is used in agreement with the word نِعْمَةٌ, or in agreement with the predicate, and it has also been read in the masculine form.

﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that the matter is so. In this there is an indication that the intended meaning of الإنسان (al-insan, man) is the species as a whole.

Qad qalaha alladhina min qablihim (Surely those before them said it): the pronoun (hā', "it") refers back to his statement, "I have been given it only on account of knowledge," because it is a word or a sentence. It is also read with the masculine (qalahu). The relative pronoun (alladhina) refers to Qarun and his people, who "said, 'I have been given it only on account of knowledge that is with me,'" and they were content with it.

Fa-ma aghna 'anhum ma kanu yaksibun (So what they had earned did not avail them): that is, of worldly wealth and what they had gathered from it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 51:

﴿So the evil consequences of what they earned afflicted them﴾, as a recompense for the evil of their deeds, or as the recompense (ajziyah) of what they earned. Its being called "evil" (sayyi'at) is because it corresponds to their evil deeds, and the recompense of an evil deed is an evil like it.

﴿And those who did wrong from among these﴾ — the polytheists — and "min" (from) is either explanatory (lil-bayan) or partitive (lil-tab'id), meaning: they went to excess in wrongdoing and transgression.

﴿The evil consequences of what they earned will afflict them﴾ — of disbelief and sins — just as it afflicted those (earlier ones). The "sin" (al-sin) here is for emphasis (lil-ta'kid), and it has indeed afflicted them, namely, an affliction whereby they were struck by drought for seven years, and their chieftains were killed on the day of Badr.

﴿And they will not escape﴾ — that is, they will not be able to flee (fa'inin).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 52:

﴿Did they not know﴾ i.e., did they say this without knowing? Or were they heedless and did not know?

﴿That Allah extends provision to whomever He wills﴾, by extending it for him, ﴿and restricts it﴾ for whomever He wills, by restricting it for him, without anyone having any role in that, when He withheld provision from them for seven years and then extended it to them for seven years.

﴿Indeed, in that﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿are signs﴾ indicating that all events are from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿For a people who believe﴾, since they are the ones who draw inferences from them to what they signify.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 53:

﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ That is: they have gone to excess in harming themselves by committing sins extensively. The attribution of "servants" (ʿibad) specifies it to the believers, according to the usage of the Noble Qur'an.

﴿Do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ That is: do not despair of His forgiveness first, nor of His bounty second.

﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ by pardon for whomever He wills, even after a while, with punishment in general and otherwise as He wills. Restricting it to repentance is contrary to the apparent meaning—how could it not be? His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ is apparent in its unrestrictedness regarding what is other than shirk. Among what indicates this is the causal clause in His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, with emphasis, and conveying exclusivity and the promise of mercy after forgiveness. The mention first of what calls for the generality of forgiveness—"My servants," which indicates humility and particularity, both of which require compassion—and the restriction of the harm of excess to themselves, and the prohibition of despair absolutely from mercy, let alone from forgiveness and its generality. Its causal reason is that Allah forgives all sins. The placing of the noble Name in place of the pronoun (p-260) indicates that He is the One who is self-sufficient and the Bestower absolutely. The emphasis with "all" (jamiʿan), and what is narrated of the occasions of revelation indicating that the verse was revealed concerning those who repented, do not require restricting the ruling to them. The obligation of applying the unrestricted to the restricted within a single statement, as in: "The most excellent of the virtuous are the most honorable of the perfect," is not accepted; so how much more so regarding what is in the position of a single statement? That does not undermine the command to repentance and sincerity in His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And turn back in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped﴾. For the claim is not that the verse indicates that forgiveness is attained by everyone without repentance, and without a prior punishment, so as to render the commands to both of them unnecessary and to contradict the threat of punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 55:

﴿And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. That is: the Qur'an; or what has been commanded, rather than what has been forbidden; or the strict obligations (ʿazaʾim) rather than the concessions (rukhas); or the abrogating (nasikh) rather than the abrogated (mansukh). And perhaps it is what is more conducive to deliverance and safety, such as turning back (to God) in repentance and persistence in obedience.

﴿Before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾, by its coming, so that you may make amends and prepare for it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 56:

﴿Lest a soul should say﴾, i.e., lest it [should] say. The indefinite form (nakrah) "a soul" is for multiplicity, as in His saying, ﴿a soul shall know what it has presented﴾, for this is a mode of expression that is often used when the intention is to indicate multiplicity and generality. Its verification has already been discussed at the beginning of Surah al-Hijr.

﴿Alas for me!﴾ (ya hasrata), with an alif replacing the ya' of possession. It has also been read as "ya hasratah" with the silent ha' (ha' al-sakt) in pause, and as "ya hasratayya", combining the two substitutes (al-'iwadayn), and as "ya hasrati" in its original form. The meaning is: "Come forth, for this is the time of your presence."

﴿Over what I neglected﴾, i.e., over my neglect and my shortcoming ﴿in regard to Allah﴾, i.e., in His side, in His right, and in His obedience. Upon this is the saying of the one who said:

"Do you not fear Allah regarding one who loves you, whose liver is burning and whose eye is brimming with tears?"

This is a kinaya (metaphor/allusion) which contains exaggeration. It has also been said: "in the essence of Allah", with an omitted noun, such as "obedience". It has also been said: "in His nearness", from His saying, ﴿and the companion at the side﴾. It has also been read: "in the remembrance of Allah".

﴿And indeed I was among the mockers﴾, i.e., among those who ridiculed the religion of Allah the Exalted and its people. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: "I neglected while I was a mocker."

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 57:

﴿Or (lest) it say, "Had Allah guided me, I would have been among the righteous (al-muttaqun)."﴾ [guided me] by directing me to the truth, ﴿I would have been among the righteous﴾ who avoid shirk and sins.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 58:

﴿Or [that] it say, when it sees the punishment: "If only I had a return [to the world]"﴾ — a return (raj'ah) to the worldly life — ﴿so that I might be among the good-doers﴾ in belief (al-'aqidah) and action. And "or" (aw) is for indicating that they are not free of these statements, out of regret (tahassur), bewilderment (tahayyur), and making excuses (ta'allul) with what has no benefit in it. And His, exalted be He, saying:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 59:

﴿Yes, indeed My signs came to you, but you denied them, grew arrogant, and were among the disbelievers.﴾ This is a refutation from Allah Most High directed at him, concerning what his statement "Had Allah guided me..." contains of the meaning of negation, and [the refutation is] separate from it (p-261), because placing it [the affirmation "Yes"] before it would split the connected phrases, and delaying the thing being refuted would disrupt the existential order; for he [the speaker] first feels regret over his negligence, then makes an excuse by the absence of guidance, then wishes for a return. [This refutation] does not negate the effect of Allah's power on the act of the servant, nor the attribution of the act to him, as you have understood. The address is masculine in consideration of the meaning (ta'dhir al-khitab bi-i'tibar al-ma'na), and it has also been read with the feminine (ta'nith) form (qur'a bi-al-ta'nith).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 60:

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah﴾ by ascribing to Him what does not befit His majesty, such as taking a son, ﴿their faces blackened.﴾ This is due to the severity that befalls them, or due to the darkness of ignorance that appears to be upon their faces. The clause is a circumstantial clause (hal), in which the pronoun has been sufficient without the waw (of circumstance), on the basis that the seeing (ru'yah) is visual (basariyyah), or that it is a second object of it on the basis that it is cognitive (irfaniyyah).

﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling﴾ i.e., a place of abode (maqam)?

﴿for the arrogant?﴾ — those who were arrogant towards faith and obedience. This is an affirmation of what precedes it, namely their being seen in this state.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 61:

﴿And Allah will save those who have been mindful of God﴾ (ittaqaw), i.e., [who avoided] shirk and sins, namely from Jahannam (Hellfire). It is also read as "yunjī" (يُنْجِي), from al-injā' (الإنْجاء, causing to be saved).

﴿with their salvation﴾ (bi-mafāzatihim): a mimi noun (maṣdar mīmī, a verbal noun beginning with mīm), derived either from fāza bil-maṭlūb (فاز بالمطلوب), meaning he attained the sought object, i.e., prospered in it. The "bā'" (الباء, the preposition "bi-") is connected to an omitted element that is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) of the relative pronoun (al-mawṣūl), conveying the simultaneity of their being saved from the punishment with their attainment of the reward. That is, Allah the Exalted will save them from the abode of the arrogant while they are accompanied by their success in their sought goal, which is Paradise.

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿They will not be touched by evil, nor will they grieve﴾ (lā yamassuhumu al-sū'u wa-lā hum yaḥzanūn), they are either another ḥāl of the relative pronoun, or of the pronoun in mafāzatihim, conveying that their salvation or their success in Paradise is not preceded by the touching of punishment or grief. Or [the "bā'" is] from fāza minhu (فاز منه), meaning he was saved from it, and the "bā'" here indicates accompaniment (lil-mulābasa). The statement "lā yamassuhum" (لا يمسهم) through to the end is an explanation and clarification of their salvation (mafāzatihim), that is, Allah the Exalted will save them while accompanied by their particular salvation, namely the negation of evil and grief from them. Or the "bā'" indicates causation (lil-sababiyya), either by omitting a noun (ḥadhf al-muḍāf, i.e., "by the cause of their salvation"), which is their mindfulness, as the placement of it within the relative clause suggests, or by applying the term "salvation" (mafāza) to its cause, which is mindfulness (al-taqwā). The intended meaning is not the negation of the continuation of touching and grief, but the continuation of their negation, as has been mentioned many times.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 62:

﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾, including good and evil, belief and disbelief; but not by compulsion, rather through the direct action of the one who acquires (al-kasib) their causes.

﴿And He is Guardian (Wakil) over all things﴾, disposing of them however He wills.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 63:

﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth.﴾ No one else owns their affairs or is able to dispose of them; this is an expression of His, the Exalted's, power and His preservation of them. It also indicates further that He alone is independent and autonomous, because no one enters treasuries or disposes of their contents except the one who holds their keys. (Maqalid) is the plural of (miqlid) or (miqlad), from qalladtuhu, meaning "I bound him" when I obligated him. It has also been said that it is the plural of (iqlid), an arabized form of the Persian (kilid, "key"), irregularly formed like (al-madhakir). It is related from Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, that he asked the Prophet ﷺ about the maqalid, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Their explanation is: There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I seek the forgiveness of Allah, and there is no power and no might except through Allah, the Most High, the Mighty. He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward. In His hand is the good, He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things capable." The meaning according to this is that these words belong to Allah, by which He is declared one and glorified, and they are the keys to the good of the heavens and the earth; whoever speaks them, good reaches him.

﴿As for those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, it is they who are the losers.﴾ This is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of all things and disposes of them as He wills, by giving life and causing death; the keys of the upper and lower worlds are in His hand. Those who disbelieve in His signs, both the created signs set up in the horizons and within souls, and the revealed signs of which those verses that speak to this are a part, are the losers, with a loss beyond which there is no further loss. It has also been said that it is connected to the words of the Exalted, "And Allah delivers," and what lies between them is a parenthetical digression, so reflect.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 64:

﴿Say: "Is it other than Allah that you bid me to worship, O ignorant ones?"﴾ That is: after witnessing these signs, is it other than Allah that I should worship? The phrase "tamurunni" (you bid me) is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraD) to indicate that they bade him to do so immediately after these signs, and they said: "Touch some of our gods and we will believe in your God," out of the extremity of their foolishness. It is also permissible for "ghayr" (other than) to be governed in the accusative by what is indicated by "tamurunni a'bud" (you bid me worship), since it carries the meaning of "tu'abbidununi" (you make me worship), and you say "li a'bud" (to me, worship) on the basis that its original form was "tamurunnani an a'buda" (you bid me that I worship), so "an" was deleted and what follows it was put in the nominative, as in his saying:

Ala ayyuhadha al-zajiri ahdura al-wagha... wa an ashhada al-ladhdhati hal anta mukhlidi

It is supported by the reading "a'buda" with the accusative (fatha), and it was read "tamurunani" with both nuns made explicit, following the original form, and also with the second nun deleted.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 65:

﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you﴾, i.e., of the messengers, peace be upon them.

﴿If you were to associate partners with Allah, your deeds would surely be nullified, and you would surely be among the losers﴾. This is a statement made in the manner of a supposition, in order to stir up the messengers, to make the disbelievers despair, and to announce the extreme abhorrence and ugliness of associating partners with Allah, and that it is of such a nature that the one from whom it is hardly conceivable that it could occur would be forbidden from it, so how about anyone else? The address is in the singular with regard to each individual. The first "lam" (lam al-muwatta'ah, the "preparatory lam" introducing an oath) prepares for the oath, while the other two serve for the response (the apodosis). The unqualified use of "nullification" (ihbat, the cancelling of the value of deeds) may mean that it is among their specific characteristics when they associate partners, because associating partners is more severe and more ugly coming from them; or it may be restricted to death, as has been made explicit in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless﴾. The coordination of "loss" with it is the coordination of the effect with its cause.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 66:

﴿Rather, worship Allah﴾ is a rejection of what they urged him to do. Were it not for the indication of the fronting (taqdim) of the object upon restriction (qasr), it would not be so.

﴿And be among the thankful﴾ for His favour upon you. In this there is an allusion to that which necessitates the specification (ikhtisas) and requires it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 67:

﴿They did not measure God with His true measure.﴾ They did not appreciate His greatness, may He be exalted, in their souls with its true greatness, in that they made partners for Him and described Him with what is not fitting for His sublime affairs. It is also read with the doubled consonant (tashdid).

﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand.﴾ This is an alert to the extreme of His greatness, the perfection of His power, and the insignificance of the great deeds in which imaginations are bewildered, in relation to His power, may He be exalted. It also indicates that the destruction of the world is the easiest thing for Him, in the manner of figurative representation and imagery, without considering "handful" and "right hand" literally or metaphorically, like their saying: "the forelock of the night has grayed." The "qabdah" (handful) is the single instance of grasping, used in the sense of the amount grasped in the palm; it is a verbal noun used as a name (tasmiyah bi'l-masdar), or it is understood as "possessor of a handful." It is also read in the accusative as an adverb of time (zarf), likening the time-bound to the indefinite. The emphasis of "earth" by "entirely" is because what is meant by it is the seven earths, or all of its parts, the apparent and the hidden. It is also read "mațwiyyāt" (folded), as a circumstantial state (hal), and "the heavens" is conjoined to "the earth," arranged under its ruling.

﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ How far removed and how high is He, whose power and greatness are such, above their association, or above the partners they associate with Him.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 68:

﴿And the Trumpet will be blown﴾: this is the First Blast (al-nafkhah al-ula).

﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon﴾: that is, they will fall down dead, or struck senseless (maghshiyyan 'alayhim).

﴿Except whom Allah wills﴾: it has been said they are Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, for they will not die after this; and it has been said they are the bearers of the Throne (hamalat al-'arsh).

﴿Then it will be blown again, another blast﴾: this is the Second Blast (al-nafkhah al-thaniyah), and "ukhra" (another) may be in the accusative or the nominative case.

﴿Then, behold, they will be standing﴾: standing up (qa'imun) from their graves, or waiting (mutawaqqifun). It has also been read in the accusative, on the basis that the predicate is ﴿looking (yanzurun)﴾, and this is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring back to their pronoun. The meaning: they will be turning their eyes about in all directions like those stupefied, or they will be awaiting what will be done to them.

And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord (﴿وَأشْرَقَتِ الأرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّها﴾). The light is metaphorically attributed to justice, which He established on it, because justice adorns the places and makes rights manifest, just as injustice is called darkness (ẓulmah). In a hadith: "Injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection." Therefore the Majestic Name is attributed to the pronoun of the earth. Alternatively, it means a light He created in it without the mediation of luminous bodies, and therefore it is attributed to the Majestic Name.

﴿And the Book will be placed﴾ (﴿وَوُضِعَ الكِتابُ﴾): this refers to the reckoning and the recompense, from the placing by the one who reckons of the book of accounting before him, or the pages of deeds in the hands of the workers. The singular noun of genus is used instead of the plural. It has been said: the Preserved Tablet is meant by it, and the pages are contrasted with it.

﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾ (﴿وَجِيءَ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ والشُّهَداءِ﴾) for the nations, and over them from among the angels and the believers. It has been said: the witnesses are those who bear witness.

﴿And judgment will be passed between them﴾ (﴿وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾), between the servants.

﴿With truth, and they will not be wronged﴾ (﴿بِالحَقِّ وهم لا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾) by a reduction of reward or an increase of punishment beyond what the promise has decreed.

﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, i.e., its recompense.

﴿And He is most knowing of what they do﴾, so nothing of their deeds escapes Him. And His saying, exalted is He:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 71:

﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾ . . . etc. This is a detailing of the fulfilment (tawfiyah) and an explanation of its manner, that is: they will be driven to it with violence and humiliation, in separate companies, some following others, arranged according to the ranks of their levels in misguidance and wickedness. Zumar (groups) is the plural of zumrah, and its derivation is from al-zamr, which is the sound (al-sawt), since a group is never free of it.

﴿Until when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾ so that they may enter it. Hatta (until) here is the particle after which a sentence is related, and it is also read with shaddah (hatta/haththa).

﴿And its keepers will say to them﴾ as a rebuke and reproach.

﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you﴾ of your own kind; and it is also read: (nudhur minkum, "warners from among you"). ﴿reciting to you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your day﴾ that is, this your time, which is the time of their entering the Fire. In this there is evidence that there is no obligation (taklif) before the Sharia, insofar as they gave as the reason for their rebuke the coming of the messengers and the conveying of the books.

﴿They will say: Yes﴾ indeed they came to us and warned us. ﴿But the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers﴾ when Allah the Exalted said to Iblis: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with those who follow you among them, all together﴾, and we were among those who followed him, and we denied the messengers, and we said: Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in clear falsehood.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 72:

﴿It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein."﴾ That is: your abiding therein is decreed. The vagueness of the one who says it serves to magnify what is said.

﴿So evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ The alif-lam (al) here is for the category (genus), and the one particularized by the dispraise is omitted, relying on its having been mentioned just before. That is: "So evil is their abode, Hell." What is implied by the fact that their abode being Hell is because of their arrogance toward the truth does not conflict with the fact that their entry into the Fire is due to the word of punishment having preceded against them, for it has become binding upon them only on the basis of their arrogance and disbelief. Its verification has already been discussed in the surah of Ha Mim al-Sajdah.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 73:

﴿Those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden﴾ in a manner of honor and dignity, to hasten them to the abode of generosity. It was also said: "their mounts are driven," since they are not taken there except as riders.

﴿in groups﴾, differing according to the differences in their ranks in virtue and the height of their stations.

﴿Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾. It is also read with the doubled (shaddah) form of the verb. The response of "idha" ("when") is omitted, to indicate that they will then receive kinds of honors that no expression can encompass. It is as if it were said: "until, when they reach it, and its gates have been opened."

﴿And its keepers will say to them: Peace be upon you﴾, from every disliked thing and every pain.

﴿You are good﴾, you have been purified from the filth of sins. Or it means: you are content in soul with what has been granted to you of bounty. ﴿So enter it, abiding eternally.﴾ Whatever there was of it is beyond what speech can express.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 74:

﴿And they will say: "All praise is for Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us"﴾ concerning the resurrection and the reward.

﴿And has caused us to inherit the earth﴾. They mean the place in which they settled, by way of metaphor (isti'arah). Its being inherited means its being given into their possession, with it left to them as a legacy from their deeds; or it means that they were empowered to dispose of it in the manner of an heir with regard to what he inherits.

﴿We may settle in the Garden wherever we will﴾. That is: each one of us will settle in whatever place he wishes within His vast Garden, on the understanding that therein are spiritual stations (maqamat ma'nawiyyah) which those who enter do not compete for.

﴿How excellent is the reward of those who act﴾. It is the Garden.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 39, verse 75:

﴿And you will see the angels circling﴾ (ḥāffīn), surrounding (muḥdiqīn) ﴿from around the Throne﴾, i.e., around it. The "min" (مِن) here is superfluous (mazīda), or it indicates the starting point of the circling (li-ibtidāʾ al-ḥufūf). (p-265)

﴿glorifying the praise of their Lord﴾, i.e., they declare Him far exalted above what is unfitting for Him, while being clothed in His praise. The clause is a second circumstantial clause (ḥāl, a clause describing the state of the subject) or a clause qualifying the first. The meaning is: remembering Him, the Exalted, through the two attributes of His majesty and His generosity, delighting in Him. It indicates that the highest rank of the ʿIlliyyūn (the exalted ones) and their most sublime pleasure is absorption in His affairs, mighty and majestic is He.

﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾, i.e., between the creatures, by admitting some of them to the Fire and some to the Garden; or between the angels, by settling them in their abodes according to their differing ranks.

﴿And it will be said: "All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾, i.e., for what has been judged between us with truth, and our words were placed in the station that is their due. The speakers are the believers among those who were judged between, or the angels. He omitted mentioning them because they are identified and to honour them.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Zumar, Allah will not cut off his hope on the Day of Resurrection, and He will give him the reward of those who fear."

And from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) "used to recite Banī Isrāʾīl and al-Zumar every night."
